title: Engineering electives course
titleCn: 工程专业选修课选课讨论

paragraphs.text: Part three.
You will hear two second-year students called Rick and Anita discussing the electives they can choose from on their engineering course.
First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-six.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-six.
Hi, Anita. Did you see that the information about the electives we can choose from this year has just gone up on the class website?
Really? Great. Do you want to look at it together? We better sign up as soon as possible.
I guess so, but it says on the site that we can't register any choices until three o'clock.
Oh, okay, but we need to get a move on, I think. Some people told me last year that they got turned away from a couple of the choices they wanted because they were too slow to decide.
Let's have a look at it all on my laptop then. It's pretty complicated working out which classes are compulsory and what restrictions there are on your choices.
Yes. We all have to do a language class of some kind, don't we? I think that's a really good idea.
That's not quite right. We can do a business class or a philosophy or economics one instead if we want. The required classes are thermodynamics, machine system dynamics, and mathematics.
Oh, no. I was sure we had finished with that last year.
Well, I suppose it's important for us.
Mm, guess you must be right.
So let's look at the descriptions of the topics covered by the classes we can choose from. Can you get them up on the screen?
Sure. The information also tells you how the classes are graded. Some of them have exams, but others just have classwork.
Yes, but that shouldn't influence our choices, should it? I'd say it'd be more important to try to find out how good the professor is.
True. That can make or break any class.
Well, we'll have to ask the seniors to get that kind of information.
True. I know several people have recommended the statistics class, but it would mean a very early start on Monday morning.
Well, that's not a bad thing, is it? What puts me off more is that everyone says it's very hard work.
Oh, I don't know. Not if you've done lots of stats before, and I did a special elective on it in high school. And it's very relevant, isn't it? We're bound to need it whatever work we end up doing.
Fair enough. Then there's an art and design class. My advisor said he wouldn't recommend doing that one.
Really?
Well, he said lots of people think it's an easy elective, but that actually it's very time-consuming.
I wouldn't have expected that.
Well, I thought it might be, but it's useful to know for sure, isn't it? Sometimes people's advice can make decisions even harder, but I found that really helpful.
Hmm. What I don't know is the amount of practical work each class involves. I'd like to find that out.
No, it's there. Look, if you click on that link, you'll get all that sort of information.
Great. And the class times are there too. So how do we tell them when we've made our choices?
Maybe we need to go and see our advisors. Or is there something we have to do online?
Okay. Let's go and talk to the secretary and find out.
Good idea.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-seven to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-seven to thirty.
How about thinking about the electives we did last year? Maybe that'd help us decide.
Okay.
We both did metallurgy, didn't we? It was pretty good, I think. It involved a lot of library work, but I quite enjoyed that.
Yes, it was definitely useful and well structured, but it was the most difficult class I chose. I didn't think it would be that bad.
Neither did I. But I didn't mind because some of my other electives were fairly straightforward.
Yes. Even fluid mechanics wasn't too bad.
No. The online tutorials weren't much help, but the professor made some hard stuff seem pretty easy, I thought.
Yes. He was great at simplifying concepts that were actually really hard to grasp.
Mm.
You did computing too, didn't you? What was that like?

It was okay. The later classes were much better than the earlier ones. Initially, I didn't like it much, but I liked it once we started getting more hands-on stuff. And what did you think about the energy economics course we both did?
Well, it was useful, except for the notes on the Internet. They were pretty disappointing.

Mm. I liked the way it wasn't too theoretical, though, and the fact that much of it was based on solving real problems. It really helped me get better at working through the questions we'd have to answer for our coursework.
Yes, but more input from our advisors might have been helpful, don't you think?
That is the end of part three. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers to part three.
